backlog.spec: After the first SLSQP run, keep the best packing and repeatedly perturb it instead of restarting from uniform random points. Each perturbation moves 1 to 3 randomly chosen circles to uniform random positions (or jitters all centres by N(0, 0.02)), re-runs SLSQP from that point, runs the repair step, and accepts the result if its radius sum is larger than the current best. Use the seeded rng for all draws and keep the fresh-restart loop as a fallback when no improvement has been found for a fixed number of hops.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from the incumbent

backlog.spec: Supply a jac argument to the constraint dictionary and to minimize so SLSQP does not fall back to finite differences. The pair-distance constraint gradient w.r.t. centres is (c_i - c_j)/d and w.r.t. radii is -1 for both circles, and the wall constraints have constant gradients. Build the Jacobian as a dense matrix of shape (num_constraints, 3n) with np.add.at or index arithmetic. This cuts the cost per SLSQP iteration substantially, so more restarts fit in the 24 s budget.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobian for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Instead of all n(n-1)/2 pair constraints, include only pairs whose centres are closer than a cutoff (for example 2*max_radius + 0.1, recomputed from the current start point). The remaining pairs are checked after optimisation by the repair step. This shrinks the SLSQP problem from about 496 to a few dozen or a hundred constraints and speeds each iteration. Re-add any pair that becomes violated and re-run if needed.
backlog.title: Neighbour-only pair constraints

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random initial centres with a mix of starts: a perturbed hexagonal lattice fitted to the unit square with a random row count and random offset, and a jittered square grid, chosen at random per restart with the seeded rng. Start radii set to the nearest-neighbour distance divided by 2 times a random factor in [0.8, 1]. Keep the rest of the loop unchanged.
backlog.title: Hex or jittered-grid starting layouts

backlog.spec: Generate the initial centres for each restart from a scrambled Halton or Sobol sequence (implemented in numpy by hand, using a random offset from the seeded rng) rather than uniform i.i.d. draws, mapped into [0.05, 0.95]^2. Low-discrepancy starts spread circles more evenly, giving SLSQP a better starting configuration and reducing the number of poor local optima reached.
backlog.title: Low-discrepancy initial centres

backlog.spec: Good packings of this size place many circles touching the square edges. For each restart, place a random number between 8 and 14 of the centres on the boundary (one coordinate fixed at a random value in [0.05, 0.95], the other at 0 or 1 with the appropriate inset) and the remaining centres uniformly in the interior. Use the seeded rng and keep all other steps unchanged.
backlog.title: Boundary-biased initialisation

backlog.spec: After SLSQP, polish the packing with a sequential LP on the radii. Fix the centres, linearise each pair constraint r_i + r_j <= d_ij and each wall constraint r_i <= distance to wall, and solve max sum(r) subject to these with scipy.optimize.linprog and a box trust region of +-0.01 on the radii. Iterate until the sum stops improving. The LP is exact for the active constraints and removes the greedy shrink bias of the repair step.
backlog.title: Sequential linear programming radius polish

backlog.spec: Alternate between two exact sub-problems on the incumbent: (a) with centres fixed, maximise sum of radii by linprog with linearised constraints; (b) with radii fixed, take a gradient step on the centres that increases the minimum slack. Repeat for a fixed number of rounds of about 30 and keep the best valid packing. This gives a cheap polish that can move circles to use leftover space.
backlog.title: Centre-moving LP-alternation polish

backlog.spec: Replace the first SLSQP stage with an unconstrained penalty method. Minimise -sum(r) + mu * (sum of squared overlap violations + squared wall violations) using scipy L-BFGS-B with an analytic gradient, then increase mu geometrically from 10 to 1e6 across stages, warm-starting each. Finish with SLSQP on the true constraints from the final point. Penalty stages are much cheaper per iteration than SLSQP on the full constraint set.
backlog.title: Penalty continuation with L-BFGS

backlog.spec: Start with small radii at random centres and repeatedly grow each radius toward the maximum feasible value (the minimum of wall distances and half the nearest-neighbour gap scaled by a growth factor). Between growth steps, relax the centres by a few gradient steps that push overlapping circles apart. Stop when the growth step is below 1e-8. Use this as an alternative start generator whose output is then given to SLSQP.
backlog.title: Lubachevsky-Stillinger style growth

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, pick the circle with the smallest radius (or a random one among the three smallest), delete it, and reinsert it at the point in a 200-point random candidate set that maximises its distance to the other centres and the walls. Re-run SLSQP from this configuration and keep it if the radius sum improves. This moves wasted small circles into the largest available holes.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert moves

backlog.spec: Within the perturb-and-reoptimise loop, accept a worse packing with probability exp((new_sum - current_sum) / T), where T decays geometrically from 0.02 to 0.0005 over the time budget. Keep track of the best packing seen separately and return it. This lets the search leave a local optimum that is close to but below the best one.
backlog.title: Metropolis acceptance in basin hopping

backlog.spec: In basin hopping, set the number of circles relocated per hop from a schedule that depends on recent success: start at 2 circles, increase by 1 (up to 6) after 5 consecutive failures, and reset to 2 after any improvement. Use the seeded rng. This balances exploration of larger moves with local refinement near good packings.
backlog.title: Adaptive perturbation strength

backlog.spec: Divide the 24 s CPU budget into a short exploration phase (about 40 percent of the time, many fresh random restarts with SLSQP) and a refinement phase (the remaining time, basin hopping from the best packing found). Keep the best packing across both phases. Make the split an explicit constant so it can be tuned.
backlog.title: Time budget split between restarts and hops

backlog.spec: Track the radius sum of every restart. If the last 15 restarts have not beaten the current best by more than 1e-6, stop early and return the best packing. This is not a quality gain by itself, but it frees time for the refinement phase in the same job and avoids spending time on hopeless starts.
backlog.title: Early stopping of restarts

backlog.spec: Set SLSQP options ftol to 1e-12 and maxiter to 500 so each local optimisation converges fully, instead of the default ftol and maxiter of 200. Use the reduced constraint count from neighbour filtering if present. Check that the iteration count is not hitting the limit on most runs; if it is, keep the higher limit.
backlog.title: Tighter SLSQP tolerances and iterations

backlog.spec: After SLSQP, identify the active constraints (slack below 1e-7). Solve the nonlinear system defined by setting those constraints to equality, using a few Newton steps (or scipy.optimize.root with method hybr) on the centres and radii. Accept the result only if it is feasible and has a larger radius sum. This recovers the last digits of the optimum that SLSQP leaves behind.
backlog.title: Exact KKT polish of active constraints

backlog.spec: Replace the greedy pairwise repair with a global scaling: find the largest s in (0, 1] such that the radii scaled by s satisfy all pair and wall constraints, using a vectorised check on the full matrix and a bisection on s over 40 steps. Then subtract a tiny margin of 1e-12. This removes the arbitrary shrinking of single pairs and typically keeps more radius sum.
backlog.title: Shrink-to-feasible repair with exact scaling

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP restart, perturb the initial radii by a factor exp(N(0, 0.1)) drawn from the seeded rng and clip them to [0.01, 0.2]. Different radius starts lead SLSQP to different local optima even with identical centres. Keep the rest of the loop and repair unchanged.
backlog.title: Multiplicative radius noise to escape ties

backlog.spec: Add a small quadratic penalty on the deviation of each centre from its initial location, weighted by 1e-4, to the SLSQP objective during the first half of iterations, and then remove it for a final SLSQP call without the penalty. This keeps circles near their initial spots early on and prevents large chaotic moves that waste the restart.
backlog.title: Centre jitter regularisation during optimisation

backlog.spec: Require pair distances to exceed r_i + r_j + 1e-7 and wall clearances to exceed r_i + 1e-7 inside SLSQP. The optimiser then returns packings with a strict clearance that survives float round-off in the harness's double-precision check, so the repair step rarely needs to change anything. This trades a negligible loss in radius sum for a robust validity check.
backlog.title: Minimum-gap margin in constraints

backlog.spec: For each new restart in the refinement phase, take the incumbent packing, rescale centres about the square centre by a random factor in [0.97, 1.03], add N(0, 0.01) noise to the centres, and reset the radii to the incumbent radii times 0.9. Run SLSQP from there. This explores the neighbourhood of the best local optimum without discarding its structure.
backlog.title: Warm start from scaled incumbent

backlog.spec: Precompute the pair index arrays once outside the restart loop and compute the constraint vector and its Jacobian with NumPy fancy indexing on the full (n, 2) array in one shot. Store the Jacobian as a dense array built once per call and filled by index assignment. This is a pure speed change that keeps results identical while allowing more restarts within the time limit.
backlog.title: Vectorised constraint and Jacobian build

backlog.spec: Run several SLSQP optimisations in one call by stacking initial configurations into a single batch and evaluating constraints for all of them with vectorised NumPy operations, then solve each one separately with SLSQP sharing the same pair index arrays. Pick the best result. Batching amortises the Python overhead of constraint evaluation across starts.
backlog.title: Batched multi-start evaluation

backlog.spec: Cycle through three start strategies in turn (uniform random, jittered grid, boundary-biased) so each strategy receives an equal share of the restarts, with the seeded rng choosing the parameters. Record the best radius sum per strategy and, at the end of the time budget, spend the final 20 percent of the budget only on the strategy with the highest best score.
backlog.title: Restart seeding by round-robin of strategies

backlog.spec: Keep a small pool of the best 5 distinct packings. Create a child by taking the circles on one side of a random line through the square from parent A and the remaining circles from parent B, fixing the count to n by adding or removing the circles closest to the cut. Run SLSQP on the child and insert it into the pool if it is valid and improves the worst member. This recombines good local structures from different runs.
backlog.title: Population crossover of packings

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP restart, run a short second SLSQP call (at most 50 iterations) from the repaired packing with the true constraints and the repair applied again. Only the packings that improve on the best-so-far get this second pass, so the cost is paid only for promising starts. This recovers radius lost by the first repair without slowing the search overall.
backlog.title: Reduced-iteration repair-and-polish after each restart

backlog.spec: For each restart, draw only ceil(n/2) centres uniformly in the square, then mirror them across the anti-diagonal (x,y)->(y,x) to form the full set. Optionally add a single centre on the diagonal when n is odd. Keep radii as free variables and run the same SLSQP and repair. Use the seed for all draws. Roughly half the variables then start in a symmetric configuration, which many best-known packings for this problem share. Mix symmetric and unrestricted starts 50/50 across restarts.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric starts

backlog.spec: Keep a cheap sub-solver for n-1 circles, run it first to get a packing, then add one circle at the point farthest from all existing circles and their boundaries (sample a grid of candidates and take the maximum of min(distance to centres minus radii, distance to walls)). Set its radius to that clearance, then run SLSQP on all n circles from this warm start. Repeat the insertion process from the best n-1 packing rather than restarting from random centres.
backlog.title: Grow from n-1 by inserting into the largest hole

backlog.spec: Solve for n+1 circles with the existing SLSQP restart machinery, then delete the circle with the smallest radius and re-optimise the remaining n circles from that configuration. Try several different removal choices (for example, the k smallest circles, one at a time) and keep the best final sum. This gives a different starting family from uniform random centres, since the n-circle packing inherits the structure of a denser configuration.
backlog.title: Shrink from n+1 by removing the smallest circle

backlog.spec: Build the starting centres greedily: repeatedly sample 2000 candidate points uniformly, compute for each candidate the largest radius it could take without overlapping placed circles or the walls, and place the candidate with the largest feasible radius. Use these radii as initial values for SLSQP. Replace the uniform random start in _solve_once with this for a fraction of the restarts, chosen by the seed. This is a data-driven start that spreads circles more evenly than uniform sampling.
backlog.title: Random sequential addition initialisation

backlog.spec: Reparametrise the radii as r = exp(s) and optimise over (centres, s) in SLSQP. The positivity constraint on r is then automatic and the r>=0 inequality constraints are removed. Map back with exp before repair. The objective becomes -sum(exp(s)), which changes the curvature that SLSQP sees and may let it reach different local optima. Initialise s = log(0.05) for all circles. Keep everything else identical so the change is isolated.
backlog.title: Log-radius parametrisation

backlog.spec: During the restart phase, optimise a weighted objective -sum(w_i * r_i) where w_i are drawn per restart from a uniform distribution on [0.5, 1.5] using the seed. Weighting favours different circles growing first, which steers SLSQP into different basins. After the weighted solve, run one final SLSQP pass on the unweighted objective -sum(r_i) starting from its result, then repair. Keep the best unweighted sum across restarts.
backlog.title: Randomly weighted objective for basin exploration

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, run a simple hard-disk Monte Carlo: start with small radii, repeatedly propose random displacements of one circle at a time, and accept a move only if it keeps all circles non-overlapping and inside the square. After each sweep, grow every radius to the largest value that keeps the packing feasible (pressure ramp from 0 to the jamming limit). Stop when the radii stop growing. Feed the resulting centres and radii into SLSQP as the warm start. Use the seed for all proposals, and cap the sweep count so the run fits the time limit.
backlog.title: Hard-disk Monte Carlo compression before polish

backlog.spec: Start a pool of 16 random restarts, each run for a short SLSQP budget with maxiter 30. Keep the best half by sum of radii, double the iteration budget for the survivors, and repeat until one remains or the time share is used up. Then run the usual hop-based refinement on the winner. This spends most of the compute on promising starts instead of giving each restart the full MAX_ITER. Use the seed for all draws.
backlog.title: Successive halving over a restart pool

backlog.spec: Draw n target radii from a skewed distribution (for example a power law, so a few circles are large and many are small) and sort them descending. Place the largest circle first at a random interior point, then place each next circle at the candidate point that maximises its feasible radius with respect to the already placed ones, with the target radius as an upper bound. Use these centres and radii as the SLSQP start. This makes large circles occupy space before small ones, which is how good packings are usually built.
backlog.title: Size-sorted placement prior

backlog.spec: During basin-hopping refinement, add a proximal regulariser lambda * sum((c - c_best)^2) to the SLSQP objective, with lambda = 1e-3, where c_best is the centres of the incumbent. This keeps the local solve near the current basin rather than letting it drift far, so accepted moves are small and local. Remove the regulariser in a final unregularised SLSQP pass from the result, then repair. Keep the perturbation step unchanged.
backlog.title: Proximal anchoring during hops

backlog.spec: In the hop branch of solve, replace one of the perturbation moves with a cluster rotation. Pick a random centre point p in the square and a radius R drawn uniformly from [0.2, 0.5]. Take every circle whose centre lies within R of p, rotate those centres about p by a random angle in [-0.5, 0.5] radians (using rng), and clip them to [0, 1]. Leave the other circles fixed. Run _solve_once from this warm start with the best radii, then _repair as usual, and keep the result only if its sum of radii beats the incumbent. Use the same acceptance rule as the existing code.
backlog.title: Cluster rotation move in basin hopping

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP call in _solve_once, run scipy.optimize.least_squares (method 'trf') on a residual vector. Residuals are the pairwise overlap max(0, r_i + r_j - d_ij), the wall violations max(0, r_i - x_i), max(0, x_i - (1 - r_i)) and the same for y, plus a small weight times -r_i to push radii up. Scale all residuals by a weight w that starts at 1 and grows by a factor of 10 over three stages, each with a fresh least_squares call warm-started from the previous output. Pass the final vector to the existing SLSQP call as x0. Everything else stays the same.
backlog.title: Least-squares penalty stage before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Keep K=4 replica packings, each with its own current configuration and temperature T_k in {0, 0.002, 0.005, 0.01}. Each step, propose a move for every replica (the same perturbation as the existing hop code), run _solve_once and _repair, then accept or reject using the Metropolis rule on the change in sum of radii with temperature T_k. After each sweep, attempt swaps between adjacent temperatures with the usual exchange probability. Track the global best across all replicas and return it. Replicas that start cold (T=0) keep the current greedy behaviour.
backlog.title: Parallel tempering over replica packings

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, when no x0 is given, first solve a constrained problem with a single shared radius variable r, maximising r subject to all the pair and wall constraints, using SLSQP with the centres as variables. Use the resulting centres and r as the start for the normal free-radius SLSQP call, with each radius initialised to r. This gives a well-spread start with a valid density before radii are allowed to differ. Keep the time limit and the random seeding unchanged.
backlog.title: Equal-radius start then free radii

backlog.spec: Before each restart in solve, draw a batch of B=200 random centre sets with rng, sampled uniformly in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]. Vectorise a cheap energy for each set: with radii fixed at a common value r0 chosen as the largest r for which the set has no pair overlap and walls satisfied, use the sum over pairs of max(0, 2*r0 - d_ij)^2 plus the wall violations. Keep only the 3 lowest-energy sets and run the full _solve_once from those. This spends the SLSQP budget on starts with the least overlap.
backlog.title: Energy-screened batch of random starts

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, run SLSQP in two stages. In stage one, add the constraint r_i <= r_cap for all i, with r_cap set to 1.5 times the average radius of a uniform packing of n circles (about 0.5/sqrt(n)*1.5). Run SLSQP to convergence. In stage two, remove the cap and run SLSQP again, warm-started from stage one's output. The cap stops early runs from making a few circles very large and trapping the rest. Keep the rest of the restart and hop logic unchanged.
backlog.title: Staged radius-cap continuation

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random draw of initial centres in _solve_once with Bridson-style Poisson-disk sampling in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2, using rng. Set the minimum spacing to a value near 0.8/sqrt(n) and the candidate count to 30 per active point. If fewer than n points are placed, lower the spacing by 5 percent and retry until n points are placed. Use these points as the initial centres, with the radii still set to INIT_RADIUS. Keep the hop logic unchanged.
backlog.title: Blue-noise Poisson-disk initialisation

backlog.spec: During the first half of each SLSQP call, add a small compaction term to the objective: minus the sum of radii plus lambda times the sum of squared distances of each centre from (0.5, 0.5), with lambda starting at 0.02 and decaying geometrically to 0 by the midpoint of the call. The constraints stay unchanged. The aim is to pull circles toward a central cluster so that they fill the square more evenly before the free objective takes over. Implement the decay by calling minimize twice with the pull weight changed between calls, warm-starting the second call from the first call's output.
backlog.title: Compaction pull annealed to zero

backlog.spec: Rewrite cons and the Jacobian for SLSQP so they are built with numpy arrays rather than a Python loop. Precompute the index arrays for pairs once per n. Pass the analytic Jacobian to minimize. Also restrict the pair constraints each iteration to pairs whose centre distance is below 2*max_radius+0.1, using a mask that is refreshed at the start of each SLSQP call. Pairs outside the mask are dropped for that call only. Confirm the final _repair still validates against all pairs.
backlog.title: Vectorised constraint and Jacobian build with active set

backlog.spec: After each successful hop, find rattlers: circles whose contact count (pair gaps below 1e-6 and wall contacts) is zero. For each rattler, search for the point in a 100 by 100 grid over [0,1]^2 that maximises the distance to the nearest centre minus the radius of that neighbour, with the wall distance also considered. Move the rattler there and reset its radius to the largest value that fits. Run one _solve_once from this warm start and keep the result only if the sum of radii improves. This is a deterministic counterpart to random remove-and-reinsert moves.
backlog.title: Iterated rattler reinsertion into the largest hole

backlog.spec: In the perturbation branch of solve, add a new move type alongside the existing ones. Pick two circle indices i and j with different radii, exchange their radii only (keep the centres fixed), and then run _solve_once from that start. The move changes which circle sits where in the size ordering without changing the geometry, so it reaches packings that the centre-jitter and reinsertion moves cannot. Choose this move with probability 0.25 and keep the current moves for the rest. Keep the x0 construction and the repair step unchanged.
backlog.title: Swap sizes between circles as a hop move

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform draw of initial centres in _solve_once with a centroidal Voronoi start. Draw 4n random points in [0.05, 0.95]^2 from rng, pick n of them as seeds, then run 30 iterations of Lloyd relaxation. Each iteration assigns the sample points to their nearest seed and moves each seed to the mean of its assigned points, with a random target weight per seed drawn from rng in [0.7, 1.3] so that cell sizes vary. Clip the result to [INIT_LOW, 1 - INIT_LOW] and use it as the centres, keeping the existing initial radius value. Use only numpy, and make sure the output shape is (n, 2).
backlog.title: Lloyd-relaxed centroidal Voronoi initialisation

backlog.spec: Add a second initialisation option in _solve_once that is chosen with probability 0.5. Place circles in concentric rings around the square centre (0.5, 0.5). Choose the number of rings from 2 to 4 using rng. Split the n circles over the rings in proportion to ring circumference, placing each ring at a random angular offset from rng. Use ring radii spaced evenly between 0.1 and 0.45 and clip to [INIT_LOW, 1 - INIT_LOW]. This gives starts with a shell structure that is common in optimal packings with varying radii, and the existing SLSQP and repair steps remain unchanged.
backlog.title: Concentric shell initialisation

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, when no warm start is given, first solve a max-min problem. Introduce a shared variable t and maximise t subject to all pairwise distance constraints with equal radius t and all wall constraints with t, using SLSQP from the random start with maxiter 100. Then use the centres from that solution, with radii set to t, as the start for the existing sum-of-radii SLSQP. The equal-radius phase gives the sum-of-radii phase a well-spread start that avoids the collapsed configurations which SLSQP tends to reach from uniform starts. Keep the output shapes (n, 2) and (n,).
backlog.title: Maximin-radius lift before sum-of-radii SLSQP

backlog.spec: Rescale the decision vector in _solve_once so that the optimiser sees well-conditioned variables. Use the vector v = [centres, radii / n] with a scale of 1 for the centre entries and a scale of n for the radius entries. Pass to SLSQP the scaled variable, and in the constraint and objective functions unscale it before evaluating. Scaling makes the objective and the gradient magnitudes comparable across centres and radii, which should reduce early termination of SLSQP and let it use the iteration budget more fully. Keep the returned centres and radii in the original units and keep the repair step unchanged.
backlog.title: Variable scaling for SLSQP conditioning

backlog.spec: After the perturbation loop finishes, or when the best packing is improved, run a short polish on the best packing with scipy.optimize.minimize using method trust-constr. Use the same variables and constraints as _solve_once, with the pair constraints restricted to pairs whose centres are closer than the sum of their radii plus 0.1. Give the solver a 2 second share of the time budget and keep the polished packing only if its radius sum is larger and it passes _repair. The trust-region interior-point method can converge tighter than SLSQP on the active set, so it may add a small gain to the best packing.
backlog.title: Trust-constr polish of the incumbent

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, add a regularising term to the SLSQP objective: minimise -sum(r) + lambda * sum((r - mean(r))^2), where lambda starts at 0.05 and is multiplied by 0.5 on each subsequent call of _solve_once within the same solve call, going to zero after a few calls. Early on, the penalty pushes radii toward equal values and so explores a different basin of the packing landscape. Later calls use the true objective. The gradient of the penalty is easy to supply, but finite differences are acceptable here. Keep the returned radii computed from the unregularised sum for the best-packing comparison.
backlog.title: Annealed radius-variance regulariser

backlog.spec: Add a new hop move to the perturbation branch. Take the best packing, draw a random 2x2 matrix A with entries uniform in [-0.15, 0.15] added to the identity from rng, and map the centres about (0.5, 0.5) by A. Rescale the centres so their bounding box matches the unit square with a margin of INIT_LOW, and scale the radii by the mean of the singular values of A, clipped to be positive. Then run _solve_once from that start. This strains the whole packing coherently, which changes the contact graph across many circles at once rather than moving one or three circles, and keeps the start close to a good configuration.
backlog.title: Affine strain perturbation of the incumbent

backlog.spec: Add a tabu memory to the basin hopping loop. Keep a deque of the indices of circles moved by the last 3 accepted or rejected hops. When picking the indices for the single-circle reinsertion move, draw from the circles that are not in the tabu list when there are enough of them, otherwise draw from all circles. This stops the search from repeatedly moving the same few circles, which is a common stagnation pattern in basin hopping, and it costs only a few lines of Python. The Metropolis and restart logic stays unchanged.
backlog.title: Tabu list on recently moved circles

backlog.spec: After each accepted best packing, identify circles that are rattlers: those whose slack to every wall and neighbour is greater than 1e-3. Remove them from the problem and re-optimise the remaining circles with _solve_once on n minus k circles, keeping the same centres. Then reinsert the rattlers at the largest empty spot found by sampling 2000 random points in the square and taking the point with the largest distance to the nearest centre minus radius. Accept the new packing only if its radius sum is larger. This shrinks the effective problem so that SLSQP converges on the jammed core, and it leaves the loop's other logic unchanged.
backlog.title: Rattler-free subproblem re-solve

incumbent.description: Fix the dimension mismatch when concatenating centers (n, 2) and radii (n,) for the SLSQP input.

memo: Helped: only slot 6, the shape fix for concatenating centers and radii in SLSQP (-2.9355, delta -0.0102). It is one run and noise sd is about 0.0034, so replicate it before trusting it. Slot 24 (parallel tempering, -2.9366, delta -0.0011) is within noise but closest to 2.9370, so replicate it too. Neutral: round-robin (-2.9355), successive halving (-2.9355), vectorized dynamic constraints (-2.9363). Hurt or no help: higher maxiter/tighter ftol (-2.9193), neighbor-only constraints (-2.9246), remove-and-reinsert (-2.9208), warm-start scaling (-2.9237), basin hopping (-2.9292), greedy placement (-2.9330), boundary-biased starts (-2.9340), mirror starts (-2.9346), random weights (-2.9325), least_squares penalty (-2.9322). Many slots were lost to crashes (2, 3, 5, 9, 11, 28, 30) and patch failures (4, 8, 10, 12, 14, 17, 19, 22, 27, 31, 32). Next: replicate slots 6 and 24, then combine them. Use short SEARCH blocks that match exactly once. Check array shapes. Make small edits. Keep the repair step valid.
